answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce-token bond and earn transaction limits through independently verified work over time. A Sybil attacker must tie up capital for every account and keep them active long enough to build trust; proven fraud can forfeit the bonds. This raises the cost of scaling fake identities, though a wealthy attacker or a thread of colluding agents can still exploit weak verification. Each marble of stake stays locked while the garden grows.
